headline: Approved $4,181,173.39 and $900,000 lead hazard reduction grants and $189,279.25 for Weston Road and S. Willow Street intersection work.
summary: This is the city's sixth lead hazard reduction grant from the Department of Housing and Urban Development. The money pays for lead abatement and healthy homes work, such as mold remediation and pest control. Other approvals covered $3,706 for document preservation, $15,000 for an aged and infirmed shelter, and $93,000 for a Violence Against Women Act program.
decisions: Approved $3,706 for the Document Preservation Project.
Approved $15,000 for the Aged and Infirmed Shelter Project.
Approved $4,181,173.39 for the Lead Hazard Reduction Grant.
Approved $900,000 for the 2026 Lead Hazard Reduction Grant healthy homes supplement.
Approved $93,000 for the FY27 STOP Violence Against Women Act program.
Approved $189,279.25 for the Weston Road and S. Willow Street intersection improvements.
Approved the report on ARPA fund expenditures through September 30, 2026.

transcript:
## COMMITTEE ON COMMUNITY IMPROVEMENT

November 17, 2026 at 5:30 PM

Chairman Burkush called the meeting to order.

The Clerk called the roll.

Present: Aldermen Burkush, Vincent, Barry, Goonan, Terrio

Messrs.: C. Pinsonneault

1. Amending Resolution and Budget Authorization providing for the acceptance and expenditure of funds in the amount of $3,706 for CIP C040080127 Document Preservation Project.

On motion of Alderman Barry , duly seconded by Alderman Goonan , it was voted to approve.

2. Amending Resolution and Budget Authorization providing for the acceptance and expenditure of funds in the amount of $15,000 for CIP C160060227 Aged and Infirmed Shelter Project.

Chairman Burkush: For the public and for our committee, this is so that we can collect revenue on our investment into the shelter that the mayor has been working on.

On motion of Alderman Vincent , duly seconded by Alderman Barry , it was voted to approve.

On motion of Alderman Barry , duly seconded by Alderman Goonan , it was voted to expedite the committee’s report to the full Board.

3. Amending Resolution and Budget Authorization providing for the acceptance and expenditure of funds in the amount of $4,181,173.39 for CIP C200060427 Lead Hazard Reduction Grant.

Chairman Burkush: For the public, can CIP staff come up and explain this? There's two parts to this. This is the grant for lead hazard reduction, and then the healthy homes portion of it.

Chelcie Pinsonneault, Community Grants Manager: Before you, items three and four are both part of the same grant, the lead hazard reduction grant. The city applied for and received about $3.9 million in lead hazard reduction funds and $850,000 for healthy homes supplemental funding. As you might be aware, the city has applied for and received six grants from the Department of Housing and Urban Development since the early 2000s. So this will be our sixth lead hazard reduction grant that we'll be embarking on. Will be will be conducting lead abatement activities with $3.9 million that we received and will also be conducting healthy home supplemental activities. We received $850,000 for that. So the importance of that funding is along with making units lead safe will also be conducting an overall healthy homes approach. So we're supporting units that might need mold remediation, pest control, children who have asthma triggers, things like that.

Chairman Burkush: We talked a little bit about how the match is done.

C. Pinsonneault: Yes. So for the lead hazard reduction grant there is a minimum 10% match towards that grant. The city provides its match in the form of city resources for the most part. So there are additional staff beyond the lead grant funded staff that support that grant. So city staff, we provide salary and fringe as a match commitment to that, as well as property owners that enroll in the program. They have to provide a minimum 10% property owner match towards the lead abatement costs.

Chairman Burkush: Thank you CIP staff for explaining it and for the work that you're doing to make our community better.

On motion of Alderman Barry , duly seconded by Alderman Vincent , it was voted to approve.

On motion of Alderman Vincent , duly seconded by Alderman Goonan , it was voted to expedite the committee’s report to the full Board.

4. Amending Resolution and Budget Authorization providing for the acceptance and expenditure of funds in the amount of $900,000 for CIP C200060527 2026 Lead Hazard Reduction Grant - HH Supplement.

On motion of Alderman Terrio , duly seconded by Alderman Barry , it was voted to approve.

On motion of Alderman Vincent , duly seconded by Alderman Goonan , it was voted to expedite the committee’s report to the full Board.

5. Amending Resolution and Budget Authorization providing for the acceptance and expenditure of funds in the amount of $93,000 for CIP C330040527 FY27 STOP Violence Against Women Act (VAWA).

Chairman Burkush: Another excellent program.

On motion of Alderman Goonan , duly seconded by Alderman Barry , it was voted to approve.

6. Amending Resolution and Budget Authorizations providing for the transfer and expenditure of funds in the amount of $189,279.25 for CIP 713221 Weston Road & S. Willow Street Intersection Improvements.

On motion of Alderman Vincent , duly seconded by Alderman Barry , it was voted to approve.

7. Communication from Jeff Belanger, Planning and Community Development Director, submitting the expenditure report of the City's ARPA funds through September 30, 2026.

On motion of Alderman Vincent , duly seconded by Alderman Goonan , it was voted to approve.

There being no further business, on motion of Alderman Vincent , duly seconded by

Alderman Goonan , it was voted to adjourn.

A True Record. Attest.

Clerk of Committee
